                    ### Question
                    A 30-year-old woman presents to her physician for her annual checkup. She has diabetes mellitus, type 1 and takes insulin regularly. She reports no incidents of elevated or low blood sugar and that she is feeling energetic and ready to face the morning every day. Her vital signs and physical are normal. On the way home from her checkup she stops by the pharmacy and picks up her prescription of insulin. Later that night she takes a dose. What is the signaling mechanism associated with this medication?

                    ### Options
                    opa. Increased permeability of the cell membrane to positively charged molecules
opb. Increased permeability of the cell membrane to negatively charged molecules
opc. Activation of tyrosine kinase
opd. Increased concentration intracellular cAMP
ope. Rapid and direct upregulation of enzyme transcription

### Enhanced Information (For Contextual Support):
Insulin binds to the insulin receptor on the cell membrane, activating tyrosine kinase. This activation triggers an intracellular signaling cascade leading to increased glucose uptake into cells and decreased blood glucose levels. The signaling mechanism associated with insulin involves the activation of tyrosine kinase.
